title: Rainy Afternoon in Nagoya Hill
subtitle: Watching droplets trace down the glass while sketching mobile UI wireframes on a napkin.
quote: Good design is not about filling space; it is about leaving room for the rain to fall.
excerpt: A sudden tropical downpour traps you inside a quiet second-story coffee shop in Nagoya. With no Wi-Fi, you take out a ballpoint pen and discover that constraints are the mother of creative flow.
body:
The Batam rain did not arrive with a polite warning.

It came as a sudden tropical curtain of silver—roaring across the metal awnings of Nagoya Hill, blurring the streetlights into radiant smears of red and amber within forty seconds.

I scrambled into a small, second-floor cafe with large floor-to-ceiling glass windows overlooking the intersection. Ten seconds later, the cafe's Wi-Fi router gave up the ghost as the neighborhood power grid flickered and shifted to backup generators.

The Joy of No Connection

With no internet connection, no Slack pings, and no Figma notifications, the silence inside the cafe felt almost sacred.

I ordered a warm cappuccino. The foam was dusted with cinnamon, radiating a sweet, comforting warmth against the chilly air-conditioned room.

I opened my physical notebook and pulled out a gel pen. For two weeks, I had been struggling with a mobile onboarding screen that felt bloated and sterile. On the screen, every component felt heavy.

I began sketching with loose, confident strokes on paper. Without auto-layout grids or pixel-snapping algorithms dictating my thoughts, the design began to breathe. I removed three redundant buttons. I opened up the white space. I moved the primary action to the bottom where the thumb naturally rests.

"When you cannot undo with Ctrl+Z, you commit to your ideas with greater intentionality."

By the time the thunderstorm cleared and the tropical sun burst through the clouds—turning the wet asphalt into shimmering mirrors—the entire user experience had been resolved on three pages of paper. Sometimes you have to lose your Wi-Fi to find your signal.
